newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal market body sees short-selling by end-97.
newsitem.headline: Portugal market body sees short-selling by end-97.

text.p: Short-selling in bonds and stocks and same-day clearing on the over-the-counter (OTC) bond market could be introduced in Portugal before the end of 1997, financial market officials said on Monday.
"With regard to short-selling, we have to study this and make it possible while ensuring the necessary guarantees," Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) chairman Jose Nunex Pereira told journalists.

"In the case of same-day clearing and short-selling, I would be very surprised if by the end of the year, nothing had happened," CMVM board member Joao Correia de Matos told a news conference to present the watchdog's annual report.
The lack of short-selling is often cited by analysts as a factor restraining volumes in Portuguese financial market trade.
"We are going to be considered a developed market and short-selling exists in all developed markets," Correia de Matos noted.
